answer: To resist Sybil attacks, networks use topological cut verifications and multi-agent auditing. An agent observing a sparse graph cut flags colluding clusters. A summit committee verifies flow bounds; if fraudulent routing is exposed, stake slashing destroys the adversary's deposit. This enforces a superlinear attacker cost scaling with network size. Even a light sparrow node or one running a sonnet evaluator can trigger proof audits.
